drivers/support_client.py — two defects encountered during HOW-0099 §7.4 Phase 4 invocation

Observed at an external project workstation (2026-05-29) invoking `bin/support file --type tooling ...`. Two defects surfaced:

1. **Title construction includes newlines.** Line 61: `title = f"[SUPPORT] [{project_id}] {ticket_type}: {description[:80]}"`. When the description starts with a paragraph followed by `\n\n` within the first 80 chars, the title contains literal newlines, which `gh issue create` rejects (the `--title` value cannot contain newlines). Reproduction: pass a description whose first paragraph is shorter than 80 chars and followed by a blank line.

2. **Hardcoded labels that don't exist on the engine repo.** Line 82: `--label "support,external-project"`. The labels `support` and `external-project` are not configured on the dz-cil repository (verified via `gh label list --repo pltrinh1122/dz-cil` — present labels include `backlog`, `bug`, `documentation`, `enhancement`, status/path/loop/area/sg families, but no `support` or `external-project`). `gh issue create` fails with a missing-label error.

Proposed fix:
- For (1): split on the first line — `first_line = description.strip().splitlines()[0] if description.strip() else ticket_type` then `title = f"[SUPPORT] [{project_id}] {ticket_type}: {first_line[:80]}"`.
- For (2): either configure the labels on the dz-cil repo (operator action) or remove the `--label` argument from the gh invocation. The issue-title bucket already provides type categorization, so the label may be redundant.

Severity: blocking — the tool is the canonical HOW-0099 mechanism and currently fails for any non-trivial ticket body. A local patch was applied at the external workstation to enable the Phase 4 wave; that patch is not pushed.

## Request

AMEND-U-003: HOW-0099 §4.2 Digest Format — codify Digest-as-index-not-duplicate authoring choice

§4.2 specifies the "sectioned monolith" format with addressable IDs (INV-NNN / CONV-NNN / AP-NNN / ARCH-NNN / TOOL-NNN) but does not address whether the Digest should restate rule text verbatim from source governance docs or simply cite (file + line range) + brief paraphrase.

The Digest-as-index pattern (cite, don't duplicate) has a notable advantage: it avoids creating a cross-branch byte-identity obligation on the underlying rule text in projects that enforce governance-paths parity (a common pattern where governance docs must remain byte-identical across active branches). It also keeps the source document as single source of truth — when the source line moves or text changes, the Digest update is bounded to a citation-line update, not a full rule-text re-sync.

Proposed amendment: §4.2 adds a sub-section "Recommended: Digest entries cite source-of-truth (file + line range) with brief paraphrase rather than restating the rule's text verbatim. This preserves the source document's single-source-of-truth status and avoids creating multi-branch parity obligations on Digest content." With a worked example showing an entry format like:

    ### INV-NNN — Short label
    **Source**: <file>:<line>
    **Rule**: <brief paraphrase>
    **Why**: <one-line rationale>
    **Status**: blocking | advisory

## Request

GAP-U-002: Append-only history enforcement guard

An external project has codified an "append-only history" doctrine for shared remote refs: prohibited operations are `git push --force`, `git push --force-with-lease`, `git commit --amend` followed by push, `git rebase` on commits already pushed, `git reset` followed by non-fast-forward push. The doctrine treats SCM as an audit ledger: pushed refs are immutable until explicit archive-then-delete.

DZ-CIL's drivers/git_wrapper.py and bin/git do not block these operations today; the rule can only live in human-readable doctrine. Universal value: any project committed to audit-trail integrity wants enforcement at the wrapper layer rather than relying on operator/agent compliance.

Proposed surface: drivers/append_only_guard.py invoked from git_wrapper before every push/reset/rebase. Raise AppendOnlyViolation with a specific class (force_push / amend_then_push / rebase_on_pushed / reset_non_ff) and the offending command line.

Composes with the existing Abstraction Doctrine (AGENT.md §5.7) — the guard is the enforcement layer that operationalizes "all git through the wrapper" with mechanism rather than mere convention.

Priority: HIGH.

## Request

GAP-U-001: Generic worktree-path-vs-branch parity checker primitive

An external project maintaining a multi-worktree repository has codified a project-local invariant: every entry in `git worktree list` MUST have a worktree path whose tail (relative to repo root) is byte-identical to the branch ref it tracks. This concept is universal to any multi-worktree project — the "directory tail equals the ref name" parity is a content-addressable property that prevents worktree/branch confusion across concurrent sessions.

Proposed DZ-CIL surface: drivers/worktree_parity_checker.py exposing:

    def check_parity(repo_root: str, expected_alias_pattern: str | None = None) -> ParityReport

The pattern arg lets each consuming project parameterize valid path tails (e.g., a project may require a specific naming convention for working branches); without it, the checker just validates path-tail-equals-ref-name as the universal invariant.

Interface shape sketch:
    from drivers.worktree_parity_checker import check_parity
    report = check_parity(repo_root='/path/to/repo')
    if not report.is_clean:
        for v in report.violations:
            print(f"violation: worktree at {v.path} tracks {v.ref}")

Priority: HIGH (broad reuse + clean interface).

agent-meta has zero execution privileges over any other persona. It is bound by the exact same laws of physics it codified. It must queue a standard Node in the backlog, pull the issue via plan-start, branch off main, execute the repair in a sandbox, and submit a PR for operator review—exactly like any other functional agent. The Board Must Stop: You cannot fix the board while players are playing. If the loop is broken, all active nodes must be aborted, rolled back, or halted. Only when the repository state is returned to a clean baseline (origin/main with WIP=0) can agent-meta safely initiate the repair sequence. Conclusion: Granting agent-meta higher privileges to bypass the SPAO loop is an architectural crutch that attempts to solve a symptom (a bug) by destroying the cure (the invariants). The Metasystem must submit to the absolute equality of the execution loop; if it breaks, the world stops until it is fixed through standard, heavily-gated channels.

open_issues.body:
## Goal
agent-meta is the Legislature, not the Executive. What agent-meta does: It defines the philosophical and strategic rules of the game in static markdown (kb/HOW-0001-spao-execution-loop.md) and designs the orchestrator CLI schematics. What actually enforces the rules: The deterministic physics of the repository itself. If a rule exists, it must be shifted entirely out of the LLM domain and codified into stateless, hard-coded gates: The WIP-N=1 invariant isn't enforced by agent-meta scolding another agent; it's enforced by mgr_node.py instantly throwing a hard Python exception (FlowTransaction failed: Active lock exists) if a second branch is checked out. The Reflection Invariant (SG-0005) isn't enforced by an LLM asking for a retrospective; it's enforced by node_lifecycle.py mathematically blocking the spao node reflect command until artifacts/audit/retro-[ID].md exists on disk. Conclusion: agent-meta designs the chessboard. agent-platform builds the physical board based on those designs. But neither "enforces" the rules during the game. The rules are enforced by the deterministic physics of the board itself—if a piece attempts an illegal move, the board mathematically prevents it from happening. If an LLM agent ever has to manually step in to enforce hygiene or boundaries, the system's automation design has failed.
